## doxyguard-db
Queryable knowledge database over a doxygen-guard-enforced C/C++ or Python codebase.

WHAT THIS IS FOR. The index holds a repository's symbols, call relationships, threads, locks and
critical sections, dispatch, requirement links, file inventory and prose. It answers structural
questions about a symbol and its neighbours in one call where reading source takes several. It is
NOT a replacement for reading source: a question about how one name is spelled differently for
different consumers, or about the exact text of a comment, is one the index can point at but not
settle. Reading source after the index has named the file is the intended path, not a failure.

NO PERFORMANCE FIGURES ARE QUOTED HERE, deliberately. This text is served to a model that is
sometimes then graded on the answers it gives, so a number here describing which question types
the index wins teaches to the test and quietly turns a benchmark into a self-portrait. Measured
results live in the repository's committed acceptance artifacts, where a reader can check them
against the transcripts they came from.

ONE SERVER ANSWERS ABOUT ANY INDEXED REPOSITORY. Every tool takes an optional `target` — a repo
root path, or a slug. Pass it and that repository answers; omit it and the DEFAULT target answers.
The server keeps nothing between calls, so a `target` on one call never changes what the next one
sees.

The default target is DERIVED, not set: from --repo, else $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR. There is no

"""BOTH ARMS PASS `--strict-mcp-config`, AND THE SRC ARM'S IS THE LOAD-BEARING ONE. This
docstring used to claim "the src arm never sees the server at all, which is a stronger
guarantee than denying its tools". THAT CLAIM WAS FALSE, and it was false in the direction that
silently destroys the comparison.
`--strict-mcp-config` means "use ONLY the config given on this command line". WITHOUT it,
`claude -p` loads the USER'S GLOBAL MCP CONFIGURATION — and on the machine this grid runs on,
that configuration has doxyguard-db connected. So omitting `--mcp-config` for the src arm did
not remove the server; it handed the src arm the operator's own servers.
MEASURED on the p5-both run, 2026-08-15, by reading the transcripts: the SOURCE arm's context
carried the doxyguard-db instructions block, including verbatim a sentence describing a prior
measured result for the very question it was answering. `used_db_tools: 0` therefore recorded
that the src arm CHOSE not to call the index, not that it COULD not — a behavioural check
standing in for a structural one, which is the exact failure this project already recorded when
a whole grid was invalidated by validity terms that verified behaviour instead of structure.
The fix is one flag and it is unconditional. With no `--mcp-config` alongside it,
`--strict-mcp-config` yields ZERO servers, which is what the src arm's brief has always
claimed. Verified directly: `claude -p --strict-mcp-config` with no config file reports no
`mcp__` tools available, while the same invocation without the flag inherits the global set.
@brief Assemble the headless `claude -p` argv for a cell.
@return argv list.
@version 2
argv = [
"claude", "-p", prompt,
"--model", model,
"--output-format", "json",
"--add-dir", str(target),
## UNCONDITIONAL. On the mcp arm it scopes the server set to the config below; on the src
## arm it is the entire fence.
"--strict-mcp-config",
]  # fmt: skip
if arm == "mcp":
## Generated from THIS run's target rather than read from a checked-in file. The
## static file was pinned to a different repo and invalidated a whole grid.
argv += ["--mcp-config", str(mcp_config)]
return argv + permission_flags(arm)

1	# SPDX-License-Identifier: MIT
2	"""Five-tier precedence for every layered build option — ONE combination rule.
3	
4	`resolved = (tier1 or tier2 or tier5) union tier3 union tier4`
5	
6	In one line: **you can correct our guesses; you cannot un-discover a fact.**
7	
8	| tier | name | what it is | combines by |
9	|---|---|---|---|
10	| 1 | explicit | a CLI flag | REPLACES the stated layer |
11	| 2 | declared | `.doxyguard-db.yaml` / the `x-doxyguard-db` passthrough | REPLACES the stated layer |
12	| 3 | target-fact | facts someone else already wrote — a Doxyfile's ALIASES/PREDEFINED, a generator manifest, a language or platform entry point | ACCUMULATES |
13	| 4 | ecosystem | a known-ecosystem signature (UDM, ingot) | ACCUMULATES |
14	| 5 | heuristic | name-pattern matching; the floor, explicitly provisional | REPLACES the stated layer |
15	
16	WHY THIS MODULE EXISTS. "Supersede" meant three different things across the
17	pipeline, so moving one value from a declaration to a flag silently changed
18	behaviour: `cli._entry_patterns` had the flag REPLACE and the declaration EXTEND;
19	`shared_key_edges` had the declaration REPLACE; `--extra-input` APPENDS. The
20	collapse that motivated the work: passing `--entry-patterns` dropped `main`,
21	reachability collapsed, and NOTHING reported it. Under this rule a stated tier
22	can only displace the guesses, so `main` survives whatever anyone states.
23	
24	TIERS 3 AND 4 HAVE IDENTICAL COMBINATION BEHAVIOUR, and saying so is the point
25	rather than an omission. Both accumulate and both survive every stated tier, so
26	an arguable 3-vs-4 call is inert — it changes the label a reader sees and nothing
27	about the resolved set. The load-bearing distinction is 3-or-4 versus 5: calling
28	a fact a guess makes it discardable, and calling a guess a fact makes it
29	permanent. Spend the argument there.
30	
31	NOT IN `vocabulary.py`, deliberately. That module's contract is an enumerated
32	COLUMN's allowed values: a `Vocabulary` carries members, meaning and rank so the
33	DDL can ask it for a constraint clause, and a test scans the package to prove the
34	literal spelling of that clause appears in no other file. A tier is not a column —
35	the winning tier is stored in `build_meta`, whose schema is
36	`(key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT)`, so there is no clause here to generate.
37	Forcing it in would put a value set there that nothing can generate one for, which
38	is how that file starts becoming "constants". This module takes the same LEAF
39	discipline instead: `dataclasses` and `collections.abc`, no intra-package imports,
40	so `signature.py` can import it without acquiring `rich`.
41	
42	(That scan is not a hypothetical: the first draft of this docstring quoted the
43	clause keyword verbatim while explaining why the module does not use it, and the
44	test failed. A gate that reads text cannot tell an example from a usage.)
45	
46	@brief Tiered precedence and the single layered-option resolution primitive.
47	@version 1
48	"""
49	
50	from __future__ import annotations
51	
52	import json
53	from collections.abc import Iterable, Mapping, Sequence
54	from dataclasses import dataclass
55	from typing import Any
56	
57	## Tier 1 — an operator's explicit CLI flag for this one build.
58	TIER_EXPLICIT = "explicit"
59	## Tier 2 — the target repo's standing declaration.
60	TIER_DECLARED = "declared"
61	## Tier 3 — a fact someone else already wrote down (language, platform, or the
62	## target's own manifests). Accumulates; no stated tier can remove it.
63	TIER_TARGET_FACT = "target-fact"

**The rule lives in `doxyguard_db/tiers.py:1-329`**, specifically `resolve_layered()` (`doxyguard_db/tiers.py:300-335`) built on `_stated_layer()` (`doxyguard_db/tiers.py:345-358`).

### The five tiers (`doxyguard_db/tiers.py:8-14`, constants at `doxyguard_db/tiers.py:57-68`)

| tier | name | source | combines by |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `explicit` | a CLI flag | REPLACES |
| 2 | `declared` | the target repo's `.doxyguard-db.yaml` (or `x-doxyguard-db` passthrough) | REPLACES |
| 3 | `target-fact` | facts someone else already wrote (Doxyfile ALIASES/PREDEFINED, a generator manifest, a language/platform entry point) | ACCUMULATES |
| 4 | `ecosystem` | a known-ecosystem signature (e.g. UDM, ingot) | ACCUMULATES |
| 5 | `heuristic` | built-in name-pattern guesses (the floor) | REPLACES |

### The combination formula (`doxyguard_db/tiers.py:4`)

```
resolved = (tier1 or tier2 or tier5) union tier3 union tier4
```

In prose (`doxyguard_db/tiers.py:6`, `doxyguard_db/tiers.py:314-319`): tiers 1, 2, and 5 (`explicit`, `declared`, `heuristic`) are **mutually exclusive and only one wins** — pick explicit if present, else declared if present, else fall back to heuristics as the floor. Tiers 3 and 4 (`target-fact`, `ecosystem`) **always accumulate on top, regardless of which stated tier won**, and no stated tier can remove them — "you can correct our guesses; you cannot un-discover a fact" (`doxyguard_db/tiers.py:6`). The accumulating layers are placed first in the resolved order (`doxyguard_db/tiers.py:314-316`), so a target that states nothing at all resolves to exactly `(*facts, *ecosystem, *heuristics)` — the built-in default, unchanged.

Tiers 3 and 4 have **identical combination behaviour** by design (`doxyguard_db/tiers.py:24-29`) — the 3-vs-4 label only affects reporting/provenance, never the resolved set. The only load-bearing distinction is 3-or-4 (fact, permanent) versus 5 (guess, discardable).
